solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Call back to obtain a financial plan

indicators.note: back tells us the word for call is to be read from right to left

parts.note: to dub someone is to call or name them
to get something is to obtain it

explanation.surface: A request to ring someone back so as to secure a money plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' looks like a phone call but is the verb dub, to name; 'back' is the reversal indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget is an itemised forecast of income and spending, i.e. a plan for money.

clue.text: By no means wiped out

parts.note: means read as money: wiped out financially by having no money

explanation.definitionFit: A bankrupt person has been ruined financially, left with no means.

clue.text: Tucking into venison, can't be the wine pourer

indicators.note: tucking into means the second word is placed inside the first

parts.note: venison is the meat of deer
the apostrophe is dropped, leaving the letters as written

explanation.surface: Diners eating venison find there is no wine jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass vessel from which wine is poured.

clue.text: They may look right to superiors

definitions.text: They may look right to superiors

parts.words: They may look right to superiors
parts.note: the parade command '... right', turning the gaze to salute senior officers

explanation.definitionFit: On the order to look right the soldiers' organs of sight turn towards the reviewing officers.

clue.text: Nowadays, treat it as comparable with plenty

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era of dates, so it stands for nowadays
to equate things is to treat them as equal or comparable

explanation.surface: Advice that these days one thing should be likened to an abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: something adequate is sufficient, enough, so 'plenty' in the informal sense of 'that's plenty'.

clue.text: Store in which to go mad

parts.note: to depart is to go
mental is slang for mad

explanation.surface: A shop so frantic it drives you crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally: a departmental store is an old name for a department store.

clue.text: There'll be questions asked if this programme is broadcast

definitions.text: There'll be questions asked if this programme is broadcast

parts.words: There'll be questions asked if this programme is broadcast
parts.note: not a scandal raising questions but a show whose format is asking questions

explanation.definitionFit: A quiz programme is a broadcast in which contestants are asked questions.

clue.text: Publicity is about over for this handsome youth

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the word for about above is

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity
on means about, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: Fame has gone to the head of a good-looking young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the beautiful youth of Greek myth, is a byword for a handsome young man.

clue.text: Possibly run and see to make certain

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters of run and see

explanation.surface: Advice to go and check something for sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges RUN and SEE; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make sure, or certain, of it.

clue.text: Scored, but caught

definitions.meaning: ... as in notched or scratched with a cut
... as British slang for arrested by the police

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a nick is a small cut, and to be nicked is to be arrested.

clue.text: Fruit crop? It's a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in a mess, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the three letters as written

explanation.surface: A grower laments a failed harvest of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Apricots are small orange stone fruits, so they are an example of fruit.

clue.text: Simple Simon, say, gets Father Bear in trouble

indicators.note: trouble stirs things up, so the letters of Father Bear in are disturbed

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme simpleton lands a fairy-tale bear in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges FATHER BEAR IN; Simple Simon is the foolish boy of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple Simon is an example of a silly, empty-headed person.

clue.text: Band call

definitions.meaning: a circular band, as worn on a finger

explanation.definitionFit: A finger band is a ring, and British English says 'give me a ring' for a phone call.

clue.text: It beats a man with skill

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
art can mean skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Something defeats a craftsman with real talent.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ that pumps blood beats continuously, so 'it beats' describes it cryptically.

clue.text: We hear there's equal support

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is to be judged by its sound

parts.note: a peer is one's equal

explanation.surface: Gossip that someone has backing on level terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a pillar supporting an arch or bridge span.

clue.text: Fabulous writer of English soap that's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An English radio soap opera by a fanciful author.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller Aesop wrote fables, so he is a writer of fables.

clue.text: Gangs that, at heart, give one some anxiety

indicators.note: at heart means the letters are found in the middle of the words gangs that

explanation.surface: Street gangs, deep down, are a source of worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a German loanword for dread or anxiety.

clue.text: Now it holds men in premonition of evil

parts.note: the present is now

indicators.note: holds means the word it contains the following men

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sense of foreboding that grips men right now.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is a feeling that something, usually bad, is about to happen.

clue.text: One convinced of evil involved in drink

indicators.note: in signals that the jumbled word goes inside the drink

parts.note: beer is a drink

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of evil are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone sure that evil lurks in alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' is the anagram signal for evil, and 'in' is the container indicator; 'of' merely links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer is someone who holds a conviction, especially a religious faith.

clue.text: Any one of the following

parts.note: not a list heading but a member of a following, as of a cause or leader

explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter, one of a group of followers.

clue.text: Panic, having a capital depletion

definitions.meaning: to panic is to stop thinking clearly
losing one's capital, read as head, as by beheading

explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' means head here (as in capital punishment), not money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for losing composure means to panic; literally it is a beheading.

clue.text: Show where traffic goes round

definitions.meaning: a travelling entertainment with acrobats and clowns
a road junction, as in London's Piccadilly ...

explanation.definitionFit: A big-top entertainment is a circus, and in Britain a circus is also a circular road junction.

clue.text: The buck stops here

parts.note: the idiom about responsibility, reread with buck as a male rabbit going home

explanation.definitionFit: A warren is a network of rabbit burrows, where a buck rabbit lives.

clue.text: Outbreak of rain in the country

indicators.note: an outbreak scatters things, so the letters of rain are broken up

explanation.surface: Showers break out in a Middle Eastern land.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: A light across the ship

parts.note: a beam is a shaft of light

explanation.surface: A searchlight sweeps over a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam is a nautical term for at right angles to a ship's length, i.e. across it.

clue.text: Generator is put back by engineers

indicators.note: put back indicates the word is is turned round

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers return a faulty power generator.
explanation.definitionFit: To sire is to father, so a sire is one who generates offspring.

clue.text: A mistake whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: read in either direction the word is the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An error, however you view it.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is British slang for a blunder or silly mistake.

clue.text: Metal sheet used for fencing

definitions.meaning: thin metal leaf, as for wrapping food
the light sword used in the sport of fencing

explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal sheet is foil, and a foil is a blunt fencing sword.

clue.text: For an NCO such punishment may well involve stripes

definitions.meaning: a non-commissioned officer of the rank above lance-...

definitions.text: such punishment may well involve stripes
definitions.meaning: bodily punishment, like flogging, which leaves stripes on the back

explanation.walkthrough: A corporal wears two stripes on the sleeve; corporal punishment leaves stripes of another kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior army rank is corporal, and punishment of the body is called corporal.

clue.text: Art gallery for the blind

explanation.definitionFit: The Paris museum is the Louvre, and a louvre is a slatted window blind.

clue.text: Spit in the sea

parts.note: not spitting into the water but a spit, a narrow ridge of sand in the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A spit is a narrow strip of sand projecting into the sea, which is a bank of sand.

clue.text: A French wine cartel broken up

indicators.note: a cartel being broken up has its parts separated, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Bordeaux wine monopoly is dismantled.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.
